events.title: Retail sales (Oct)
events.note: Lands an hour before the 9:30 open. Let the release candle print; ICT traders often wait for the raid that follows and trade the NY AM kill zone after it.

brief.context: Retail sales rose 0.8% in September after a revised 1.3% gain in August, with gas station receipts lifted by higher fuel prices. Inflation has stayed above 3% and markets are pricing a Fed rate increase in December, so policymakers are watching whether consumer spending is holding up. This is the main read on October spending before the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.

events.recap: Retail sales came in at 0.2% against a 0.2% forecast, in line with expectations. The previous reading was 0.8%.

brief.context: The advance estimate showed the economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, above the 3.2% economists had expected, led by consumer spending. This second estimate revises that figure with more complete data. It lands the same morning as the October PCE inflation report, two weeks before the Fed's December meeting.

events.title: PCE inflation · Personal income and outlays (Oct)
events.note: Lands an hour before the 9:30 open. Let the release candle print; ICT traders often wait for the raid that follows and trade the NY AM kill zone after it.

brief.context: Core PCE prices rose 0.3% in September and 3.1% from a year earlier, up from 3.0% in August, while the headline index was up 3.6% on the year. PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, and markets are pricing a rate increase at the December 8-9 meeting. October CPI, released November 10, showed core consumer prices up 0.3% for a third straight month.
